name: Vertical Tiki-Taka 4-3-3 DM

slots.why: Sweeper keeper covers the space behind a higher line and is an extra passer.
Support wing-back on the left supplies width and joins the build-up, so this side is more attacking.
Ball-playing defender starts moves with passes into midfield.
Cover centre-back sweeps behind his partner, since the line is higher; Defend is the alternate.
Support full-back on the right stays more conservative, so the team has one more attacking flank and one safer one.
Deep-lying playmaker is the base of the team and distributes it to the runners.
Box-to-box midfielder supports the attack and the press.
Mezzala runs into the half-space to arrive in the box.
Inside forward cuts in from the left to attack the box.
Winger (Support) provides width and links with the midfield.
Lone striker: Advanced Forward runs in behind. Poacher is the alternate.

description: Short combinations are used to progress quickly rather than simply retain possession, with runners attacking spaces created by circulation.
whyGood: The playmaking DM anchors build-up while the eights and front three provide vertical movement and penetration.
whyThisShape: A 4-3-3 that combines short passing with quick, vertical moves: a playmaker sits in front of the defence, a runner and a mezzala move forward from midfield, and the forwards run in behind. It presses at once when the ball is lost.
whenToUse: When you have good passers and quick forwards, against teams that sit in a mid-block and leave space behind their line.
whenNotToUse: Against sides that press well, or when your defenders are not comfortable on the ball or with a high line.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Use short first-line outlets and midfield connections to start attacks; this asks for secure decisions under pressure.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Move the ball before the opponent resets, using the receivers and runners supplied by the roles.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Lead the mobile forwards and midfield runners into space rather than requiring every pass to arrive at their feet.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Engage the build-up earlier, accepting that the forwards need support from the midfield behind them.
instructionRationale.Higher Defensive Line: Move the back line up to reduce the space behind the midfield and support territorial pressure.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
